co_mt_blue_sky_formerly_mount_evans_mixe.approach: The summit road (Highway 5) is seasonal and closed in winter, so in the cold months the approach adds a long walk up the road or in from Echo Lake via the Chicago Lakes basin. From the Summit Lake parking area, the Crystal is a narrowing couloir below the northwest face, just right of The Snave. It sits in morning shade, so the snow stays firm longer than on the sunnier couloirs of the bowl. Crampons and an axe are the standard kit. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

The summit road (Highway 5) is seasonal and closed in winter, so in the cold months the approach adds a long walk up the road or in from Echo Lake via the Chicago Lakes basin. From the Summit Lake parking area, walk to the east end of the lake and climb into the Summit Lake bowl. The snowfield is straight ahead, a broad slope between The Snave and the Diamond Couloir, and it is not always continuous up to the ridge. It is moderate snow, with crampons and an axe. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

co_ne_buttress_hallett_peak_mixed_ice_ty.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and take the trail to Emerald Lake, roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way. At the shore, look left for the climbers' trail, then climb it up and right, contouring above the lake to the base of the big rock buttresses. Continue along the cliff base, then turn right and work up the gorge, staying slightly left of its middle to the obvious base of the couloir. The approach to the end of Tyndall Gorge is long. Snow slopes below the face can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

co_north_face_of_pike_s_peak_y_couloir.approach: The couloir starts from the Bottomless Pit below the north face. Three ways in are used: the long hike up the Barr Trail, a shorter but harder hike from the Crags trailhead, or a short descent from the toll road, which leaves no easy way back down. The Hero Traverse from the toll road also reaches the foot of the line. The line is obvious to the south; start up the main gully, and the Y branches west, to climber's right, after about a third of a mile.
